biblical_reference.note: The name of the apostle Peter, who was given this name by Jesus when he said, 'You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church.' (Matthew 16:18 NIV)

saint_reference.note: Also known as Simon Peter, the brother of Andrew and the apostle who was given the name Peter by Jesus.

data.cultural_impact: Pieter is a traditional name in the Dutch and Flemish cultures. It is a name that evokes a sense of strength, stability, and the importance of family and community in these communities. Pieter has been a popular male name for generations, and it is not uncommon for families to have many men with this name.
data.spiritual_significance: Pieter comes from the Dutch words 'piet' meaning 'little' and 'er' meaning 'rock'. The name 'Pieter' holds a spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the religious importance of the 'rock' that is God. In the Bible, Jesus refers to himself as the rock on which his church is built. Therefore, the name Pieter can be seen as a reminder of the foundation of faith in God and the importance of remaining grounded in one's spirituality. Additionally, the name can be interpreted as a call to be a meaningful and grounded individual, imparting a sense of stability and faithfulness in one's daily life.

historical_references.reference: Pieter Bruegel the Elder (1525-1569) was a Flemish painter known for his landscapes and peasant scenes.
Pieter van Houten, a character in Herman Melville's novel 'Moby-Dick', is the foster-father of Ishmael.
